bib.title: LongRAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Long-context LLMs

question: Does rebalancing RAG toward long retrieval units and a long-context reader beat retrieving many short passages?
hypothesis: Heavy-retriever/light-reader RAG is suboptimal; with long-context LLMs, long units and few retrieved items reduce hard negatives and preserve context.
contributions: Long retrieval unit (4K+ tokens by grouping or whole documents)
Long retriever returning only 1-8 units without re-ranking
Long reader prompting an off-the-shelf long-context LLM zero-shot
Ablations on unit size, recall vs EM, and reader model

method.summary: Wikipedia documents are grouped by hyperlinks into ~4K-token units (or whole long documents used as units). bge-large-en-v1.5 scores a unit by the max over chunk scores; the top 1-8 units are concatenated (~30K tokens) and fed to GPT-4o or Gemini-1.5-Pro in a two-turn prompt. Nothing is trained.

datasets.name: NQ
datasets.size: 3,610 test questions; 3M docs / 22M passages; avg doc 800 tokens
datasets.preprocessing: Grouped into 600K units via hyperlink grouping (Algorithm 1)

datasets.name: HotpotQA
datasets.size: 7,405 dev questions; 5.2M docs; avg doc 130 tokens

datasets.name: Qasper
datasets.preprocessing: Refactored from single-document QA into retrieve-then-answer, like LoCoV1

datasets.name: MultiFieldQA-en
datasets.source: LongBench; legal, government reports, encyclopedias, papers

inference.prompting: Two-turn chat: turn 1 zero-shot with full long context gives a long answer; turn 2 uses 8-shot examples to extract a short answer. Closed-book baselines use 16-shot.
inference.retrieval: Tevatron + FAISS exact inner-product index; unit score = max over chunk scores (MaxP); top k concatenated; no re-ranker. k: 4-8 grouped units, ~10 documents, ~100+ passages on NQ.

parameters.chunk_size: 512 tokens (main), 4K, or whole unit in Table 4
parameters.grouping: Algorithm 1: sort docs by hyperlink degree ascending, merge related groups while size <= S

other.note: Temperature, decoding, max tokens, seeds not stated

metrics.name: Answer Recall (AR)
metrics.definition: Answer string present in any retrieved unit that goes to the reader

metrics.name: Recall (R)
metrics.definition: HotpotQA: both gold documents are in the retrieved set

metrics.name: EM (refined)
metrics.definition: Exact match if prediction under five tokens and ground truth is a substring of prediction or vice versa

baselines: Fully-supervised RAG (REALM, DPR, RAG, RETRO, RePAQ, FiD, EMDR2, FiD-KD, R2-D2, Atlas; DrKIT, MDR, HGN, AISO, COS etc.)
Passage-level RAG on the same retriever
eval.protocol: Single run per setting, no seeds or significance tests reported; ablations use 200 test cases; baseline numbers are quoted from earlier papers.

availability.code: Project website https://tiger-ai-lab.github.io/LongRAG/ (no repo link stated in text)
availability.data: public datasets; grouped corpus release not stated

prompts.text: Go through the following context and then answer the question. The context is a list of Wikipedia documents, ordered by title: . . . . Each Wikipedia document contains a title field and a text field. The context is: "Title": . . . "Text": . . . Find the useful documents from the context, then answer the question: when did the philadelphia eagles play in the super bowl last. Answer the question directly. Your response should be very concise.

You have been provided with a question and its long answer. Your task is to derive a very concise short answer from the given long answer. It's important to ensure that the output short answer remains as simple as possible. Here a few examples: "Question": . . . "Long Answer": . . . "Short Answer": . . .
Here are some examples of questions and their corresponding answer, each with a "Question" field and an "Answer" field. Answer the question directly and don't output other thing.

results.claim: Zero-shot LongRAG with GPT-4o reaches 62.7 EM on NQ and 64.3 EM on HotpotQA with no training.
results.setup: NQ test (3,610 q) with top-4 grouped units; HotpotQA fullwiki dev (7,405 q) with top-8 units; GPT-4o reader, bge-large-en-v1.5 retriever, refined EM
results.quote: LongRAG achieves an EM of 62.7% on NQ and 64.3% on HotpotQA, which are on par
results.note: Refined EM (Appendix A.2) is more lenient than standard EM and is applied to LongRAG; baselines are quoted with their own EM.

results.claim: Grouping NQ passages into long units shrinks the corpus from 22M to 600K units and lifts top-1 answer recall from 52.24 to 71.69.
results.setup: NQ, Wikipedia Dec 2018; passage (22M units, ~120 tok) vs grouped documents (600K units, ~4K corpus avg / 6K test avg); bge-large-en-v1.5 with MaxP over 512-token chunks
results.table: Table 2, rows Passage / Grouped Documents, 1 retrieval unit, column Answer Recall (AR)

results.claim: 8 grouped-document units give AR 88.53 on NQ, about what 100 passages give (89.92).
results.setup: NQ test set; 8 grouped units (~50K tokens on test set) vs 100 passages (~14K tokens)
results.table: Table 2, row Grouped Documents 8, column AR; row Passage 100

results.claim: On HotpotQA, grouping cuts the corpus from 5.2M to 500K and lifts Recall@2 from 30.01 to 56.30 and AR@2 from 47.75 to 72.49.
results.setup: HotpotQA fullwiki, bge-large-en-v1.5; document vs grouped-document units
results.table: Table 3, rows Document 2 / Grouped Documents 2, column Recall (R)

results.claim: Encoding a long unit as the max over 512-token chunk scores beats encoding it whole with a long-embedding model (71.7 vs 23.4 AR@1).
results.setup: NQ, grouped units; BGE-Large 512-token chunks vs E5-Mistral-7B on the entire grouped unit (4000-token chunks gives 54.2)
results.table: Table 4, rows BGE-Large 512-tokens chunk and E5-Mistral-7B entire grouped retrieval unit, column AR@1

results.claim: Gemini-1.5-Pro as reader gets 58.6 EM on NQ and 57.5 on HotpotQA, below GPT-4o.
results.setup: Same retrieval as the GPT-4o run; NQ 4 units, HotpotQA 8 units

results.claim: Closed-book 16-shot baselines on NQ: GPT-4-Turbo 41.2, Gemini-1.5-Pro 47.8, Claude-3-Opus 49.2 EM; fully-supervised Atlas is 64.0.
results.setup: NQ test; Atlas figure quoted from Izacard et al. 2022
results.table: Table 5, NQ, row Atlas, column EM

results.claim: On Qasper, one 5K-token document unit gives 26.3 F1 versus 22.6 F1 for 100 passages of 200 tokens.
results.setup: Qasper (371 test cases, 416 docs) refactored to RAG; Document, 1 unit vs Passage, 100 units
results.table: Table 6, row Document 1, column Qasper; row Passage 100
results.note: Abstract and intro say 25.9 F1 on Qasper (previously 22.5) and 57.5 on MultiFieldQA-en (previously 51.2); Table 6 and Sec 3.4 give 26.3/22.6 and 57.5/51.3. 25.9 matches Document with 2 units.

results.claim: On MultiFieldQA-en, 5 long document units give 57.5 F1 versus 51.3 F1 for 100 passages.
results.setup: MultiFieldQA-en (150 cases) refactored to RAG; Document 5 units vs Passage 100 units
results.table: Table 6, row Document 5, column MutilfieldQA-en; row Passage 100

results.claim: Passage-level retrieval has high recall at 200 units (91%) yet end EM dips because of hard negatives; long units show no such drop.
results.quote: reach a marvelously high recall score (91% for recall@200). However, the end performance dips significantly

results.claim: The best context fed to the reader is around 30K tokens; past a turning point more units hurt.
results.setup: NQ ablation on 200 test cases; turning point 100-200 passages, 5-10 documents, 4-8 grouped units
results.quote: context length fed into the reader is around 30K tokens.

results.claim: Open-source DeepSeek-V2-Chat is a much weaker long reader than the five black-box LLMs; GPT-4o is best.
results.setup: NQ, 200 test cases, six readers (Fig 4 values 59.5, 61.5, 62, 61, 60, 51 percent, bar-to-model mapping not recoverable from text)
results.quote: performance degrades significantly compared to the previous five black-box LLMs.

results.claim: Reading a long retrieved context with the short-context prompt lowers performance; a two-turn long-answer then short-answer prompt works best.

limits: No training; depends on closed long-context LLMs, and open-source DeepSeek-V2-Chat degrades a lot.
Authors concede long-embedding models are weak: encoding a 6K unit whole gives AR@1 23.4 so MaxP chunking is used, and future long embedders should help.
Refined EM is lenient and applied to LongRAG, while baselines are quoted with their own metrics; Qasper and MultiFieldQA-en not compared to prior models.
Readers, decoding settings, cost and latency not reported; ablations on only 200 NQ cases; single runs.
Grouping uses Wikipedia hyperlinks, so it is not shown on corpora without link structure.

the recall of the answer string in all the retrieved documents that we plan to use in the reader
